answer: Sybil resistance comes from stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a bond under one keypair and gets voting weight from that stake, not from having more accounts. Splitting capital among fake agents buys no extra influence, yet each forgery still owes a full bond, so an attacker pays N deposits to mimic N agents and loses them all when slashing detects duplicates. It is like a karst ridge draining into one lagoon: new channels add cost, not water. Only the yarrow seed that was actually staked counts.
